title: AI on arXiv — Friday, 16 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred, curated ordering; independent attention and citation evidence is sparse for this very recent batch, so it is a notable-paper shortlist rather than a popularity ranking.

sections.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
sections.abstract: The authors train a 35B mixture-of-experts agent for long-horizon machine-learning engineering using hierarchical supervised fine-tuning and windowed interaction reinforcement learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce the Kaggle-MLE Factory and Windowed Interaction RL, reporting improved results on MLE-Bench Lite and transfer to other optimization tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline comparison is benchmark-based; it does not establish open-ended autonomous AI research beyond the evaluated tasks.

sections.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
sections.abstract: LEASH uses latent uncertainty from a weaker agent to trigger escalation to a stronger model and to monitor that model after handoff.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that LEASH reaches 73.66% task success with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B at lower estimated cost than always-on Claude Opus 5, using initial and step-level escalation plus shadow oversight.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper’s limitations state that evaluation is confined to OSWorld; its uncertainty score estimates weak-agent failure risk, not the expected gain from escalation, and the causal effect of post-handoff monitoring is not isolated.

sections.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
sections.abstract: The authors audit whether superficial cues in tool-use trajectories can predict safety labels and alter the decisions of agent guards.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors distinguish label predictability, guard association, and paired decision sensitivity, finding that trajectory formatting can change guard decisions and measured accuracy against inherited labels.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that the measured Haiku-sized effects did not reproduce with Luna or deterministic Q8 TS-Guard; the intervention cohort is small and the target labels are inherited from the underlying datasets.

sections.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
sections.abstract: MindEval2 combines psychologist-developed rubrics with a longitudinal synthetic-patient harness to evaluate language-model support across multiple sessions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that guidance calibration—not surface quality or boundaries—is the dominant remaining failure mode across the evaluated models.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports that simulated patients remain distinguishable from real users (mean realism 3.55 versus 4.20 on a five-point scale); annotation agreement is also moderate for severity and lower for individual clinical issues.

sections.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
sections.abstract: A builder agent reorganizes a raw document collection into a linked workspace before a separate answering agent handles future questions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train workspace construction as a decision process and report that anticipatory curation improves downstream answers and transfers to unseen domains.
sections.unique_caveat: The method spends effort up front to construct a workspace; its reported amortization advantage depends on reuse across queries, and results are benchmark-specific.

sections.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: LIBERO-PeRM provides five simulated task suites and paired demonstrations to test whether robot policies learn and generalize user preferences.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a controlled benchmark separating task completion from preference satisfaction and report that preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult.
sections.unique_caveat: Its preference taxonomy is limited to language-expressible choices that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal; this is not yet evidence of personalization with real users or on physical robots.

sections.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
sections.abstract: Market-based post-training jointly learns individual agent policies and the agents’ decentralized bidding for participation in a swarm.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that learning participation bids alongside action policies improves on tested coordination strategies and supports scaling and resilience to agent dropout in their experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the paper’s three evaluated task settings; performance with different agent populations, tasks, or deployment conditions remains open.

sections.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
sections.abstract: The authors use a set-level reinforcement-learning objective to train an 8B model to generate multiple document-grounded scientific ideas that are both useful and distinct.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report higher creative utility than the compared frontier systems on their benchmark, with a four-expert pilot judging the idea sets promising and similarly executable.
sections.unique_caveat: The human study involves only four experts and the paper is marked under review; benchmark utility and executable pilot ideas do not establish downstream scientific discoveries.

sections.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
sections.abstract: SoftCache turns a diffusion model’s cache-staleness signal into adaptive sampler step sizes, allowing cached steps to jump farther when estimated error is low.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose training-free soft caching, where the distance from a refresh threshold controls how far a cached sampler step advances.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison covers three model families and four fidelity metrics; broader architectures, resolutions, and quality measures remain untested in the abstract’s evidence.

sections.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
sections.abstract: Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator as a single-pass model for estimating 4D geometry and motion from monocular video.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use clean video latents with on-demand spatial and temporal queries and a frozen video-depth prior, reporting state-of-the-art or competitive results on the listed tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is limited to the reported perception tasks and monocular-video setup; the paper’s results do not establish that video generators generally provide reliable 4D perception.
